links.outcome: Accuracy under cross-validation versus leave-some-out validation on unseen participants
links.effect: Random forest cross-validation accuracy was 85.65% (SD 0.79%), but leave-some-out accuracy on unseen users was 65.70% (SD 6.6%), indicating participant-specific overfitting.
links.quote: The difference between cross‑validation and leave‑some‑out accuracies indicates participant‑specific overfitting, so the leave‑some‑out accuracy is considered the current conservative estimate of performance on unseen users and the cross-validation accuracy an estimate of potential accuracy with a more robust dataset.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an activity classification machine learning model (Random Forest) from wearable IMU sensors to support objective K-level prosthetic prescription, including exploratory qualitative interviews with prescribing clinicians.
